evals.prompt: /firststone — add my personal project music-player (https://github.com/me/music-player). This is a new laptop: ~/code does not exist yet. gh is authenticated as me; I use Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: The agent finds ~/code/personal/home missing and runs the Personal Home Repo case first. The plan lists ~/code/personal/home with AGENTS.md (one pointer line for music-player at ~/code/personal/music-player with its clone URL), CLAUDE.md holding @AGENTS.md, .gitignore listing local.md, and setup.mjs with AGENTS set to claude-code; it writes nothing before the user confirms. It then creates the private remote me/home with gh, pushes main, runs node setup.mjs, and writes the setup checklist with the line to run /setup-matt-pocock-skills from the Personal Home Repo. It writes no file inside music-player and no work-clones.md.

evals.prompt: /firststone — new work project Portal for client Acme. Team Home Repo on GitHub under the acme-team org; gh is authenticated with admin rights. Two app repos we own already exist: acme-team/portal-api and acme-team/portal-web. Colleague: Luca (luca-gh). Client contact: Sara, product owner. Granola folder: Portal. My Personal Home Repo already exists.
evals.expected_output: After the interview and a confirmed plan, the agent creates ~/code/work/acme/portal/home with AGENTS.md (skills install line, /ask-matt, two pointers under ~/code/work/acme/portal/, Granola folder: `Portal`), CLAUDE.md, docs/agents/team.md, docs/agents/constraints.md and .gitignore listing local.md and docs/meetings/transcripts/. It creates the private remote acme-team/portal-home, pushes main, then adds 'acme/portal' with its URL to work-clones.md in ~/code/personal/home and pushes there. It protects main of both app repos with PR required and zero approvals. It writes no file in either app repo, creates no GLOSSARY.md, docs/adr/ or docs/meetings/, no workflow.md and no retro label. The setup checklist tells the user to run /setup-matt-pocock-skills from the Team Home Repo.

evals.prompt: /firststone — the client of the Portal project just created a new repo for the mobile app: https://github.com/acme/portal-mobile, owned by the client. (Run from ~/code/work/acme/portal/home, created by eval 2.)
evals.expected_output: The agent recognises the App repo case in an existing Team Home Repo, reads team.md and constraints.md, and asks nothing those files answer: only what the repo is, if unknown. It adds one pointer line to AGENTS.md at ~/code/work/acme/portal/portal-mobile, commits and pushes. Because the repo is the client's and constraints.md records no client review rule, it proposes PR-required protection as an open step addressed to Sara rather than setting it. It writes nothing in portal-mobile and nothing in the Personal Home Repo.

evals.prompt: /firststone — new work project Ledger for client Fabrikam, Team Home Repo on GitHub. The client requires that all tickets live in their Jira, and their review rule is two approvals on every PR.
evals.expected_output: The agent records the tracker as Other, writes the setup checklist to docs/agents/setup-checklist.md in the Team Home Repo and prints it in chat, and helps draft the paragraph /setup-matt-pocock-skills will ask for: how a Jira ticket is created and assigned and how the five triage states are expressed. constraints.md carries the two-approval rule under Client rules. Fixed rules: every written file has content, nothing is written inside an app repo.

evals.prompt: /firststone — new work project Portal for client Acme on GitHub, one existing app repo. gh is not authenticated on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The agent detects the missing authentication itself, shows the Team Home Repo creation in the plan as a blocking open step, and after confirmation gives the link and the clicks and waits for the URL before wiring the remote with git remote add origin and a plain push. Protection of the app repo's main becomes an open step with its direct link; the setup checklist is written to docs/agents/setup-checklist.md and printed in chat. The work-clones.md line is still added to the Personal Home Repo once the URL is known.

evals.prompt: /firststone — new work project Billing for client Northwind. The client forbids keeping project material outside its infrastructure: the Team Home Repo goes on the client's Bitbucket, which I already created empty. Tracker: the client's Jira. PRs are opened on the Bitbucket site and CI runs on the client's Jenkins.
evals.expected_output: The agent pushes the Team Home Repo with plain Git, adds the open step to restrict its access to the team, and writes constraints.md with the Meeting notes section replaced by the rule that meeting notes stay out of the repo and only decisions are recorded as tickets or ADRs. The user's lines about PRs and CI appear under Client rules. It does not invent Bitbucket menu paths.

evals.prompt: /firststone — new work project Portal for client Acme on our self-hosted GitLab at git.example.com, group acme. One existing app repo, portal-api.
evals.expected_output: Every glab command targets git.example.com (GITLAB_HOST or --hostname), never gitlab.com. The agent creates acme/portal-home as a private project, pushes main, and protects portal-api's main by setting Allowed to push to no one and keeping merge for developers and maintainers, leaving required approvals at zero. It writes no .gitlab-ci.yml and no file in portal-api.
